accessibility: The tag field is required and labelled; an error is a line of text with an icon under the field, never color alone.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Panel dialog, Stack, Text, Icon, TextInput, Select, SelectOption, Button, Alert); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog.

The number of keys in "Locale (n keys)" is a baked sample, because a Select option interpolates no parameter; each error is the tag field's own invalid state and error text, which a Variant sets from a Locale key (and the language tag it suggests or names).
Every visible string is bound with $i18n except the tags typed; en-US and zh-TW keep identical key sets.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A holder of locales.write on a desktop layout pressed New Locale on the Locales page, or Create Locale on the notice that the primary Locale has no file (the tag is then the primary Locale's).
The base state is the form with the tag ja-JP typed and the keys of en-US chosen to start from.
The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme; the dialog is centered over a dimmed ground.
spec.intent: Show the New Locale dialog of the Locales page as built from Adapter Widgets only: a BCP 47 tag for the new Locale file and, optionally, the keys of an existing Locale to start from.
interactionRules: A Locale is named by its canonical BCP 47 tag: an empty tag, a tag that is not one, a non-canonical form (the canonical one is offered) and a tag the Workspace already has are each refused before anything is created.
Start with keys from copies the key names of an existing Locale with empty values, so each key shows as a reminder, or starts the file empty; without an existing Locale there is nothing to choose.
Create Locale makes the file explicitly and is busy while it works; UIUX never makes a missing Locale file on its own, and a refused creation shows its reason and keeps the form.
